title: Conversion Fees on Non-USD Payout Methods: Desk Reference and Booking Tool
content:
A transfer to a Payout Methods method whose payout currency is not USD carries one conversion fee, booked as a cross-currency fee against that method and naming the transfer it belongs to; each conversion fee is computed on the amount of the transfer it names.

## When the conversion fee falls due

The conversion fee falls due on the transfer's settlement day, the rail's processing time in business days on the business-day calendar (the US Federal Reserve holiday calendar) after the day the transfer was sent. It is booked on that day, once per transfer. A transfer returned before it settles carries no conversion fee.

| Hypothetical transfer | Sent | Rail processing time | Settlement day, when the conversion fee falls due |
|---|---|---|---|
| PayPal method paid in CAD | Thursday 2026-07-09 | 1 business day | Friday 2026-07-10 |
| Payoneer method paid in EUR | Friday 2026-07-10 | 2 business days | Tuesday 2026-07-14 |
| Payoneer method paid in GBP, returned on Thursday 2026-07-09, before its settlement day of Friday 2026-07-10 | Wednesday 2026-07-08 | 2 business days | None: a transfer returned before it settles carries no conversion fee |

## Effect of booking

Once booked, the conversion fee stands on the method's ledger as its own entry, naming the transfer, and is taken out of the method's undisbursed balance, which drops by exactly the fee. Nothing else on the method or on the transfer changes. The host sees the fee as its own line in the payout history and on the next earnings statement.

## Booking tool: `book_conversion_fee_3c5b00cd`

**Situation of use and capability.** The tool posts the conversion fee that a transfer paid out in a currency other than USD carries. One call adds one fee entry of kind `cross_currency_fee` to the payout method's ledger, dated today, naming the transfer it belongs to and carrying the amount given.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `book_conversion_fee_3c5b00cd` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `payout_method_id` | The reference number of the payout method the fee is charged against, exactly as returned by the payout-method lookup | Id |
| `source_event_id` | The reference number of the transfer record (a payout sent to the method) that the fee belongs to, exactly as shown by the payout ledger lookup | Id |
| `amount` | The conversion fee as a positive USD amount, already rounded as the fee policy prescribes | Fixed format, 2 decimal places; stored rounded to 2 decimal places and never changed otherwise |

**Return.** A text rendering of a record with `payout_txn_id` (the reference number of the new fee entry), `payout_method_id` (the method charged), `source_event_id` (the transfer the fee belongs to), `fee_type` (always `cross_currency_fee`), `amount` (the USD fee booked, 2 decimal places), `posted_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, today) and `status`. The call has succeeded when `status` comes back as "booked".

**Hypothetical illustration of a call.** For an imagined method with reference number PM-EXAMPLE and an imagined transfer record TX-EXAMPLE, a call with `payout_method_id` PM-EXAMPLE, `source_event_id` TX-EXAMPLE and `amount` 12.34 returns a receipt with `fee_type` `cross_currency_fee`, `amount` 12.34, today's `posted_date` and `status` "booked".
